question.text: A string runs over a single fixed pulley; block 1 hangs from one end and block 2 hangs from the other end.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Using the constraint (string-length) method, work out how the acceleration of block 1 relates to the acceleration of block 2.

conditions: string passes over a single fixed pulley
block 1 and block 2 each hang from one end of the string
the total length of the string is constant

figure.description: A single fixed pulley is mounted at a fixed point. A string passes over it, with block 1 hanging from one end and block 2 hanging from the other end. Taking a fixed horizontal reference line at the level of the pulley, x₁ is the distance block 1 hangs below this line and x₂ is the distance block 2 hangs below this line; because the total string length is fixed, as one block moves down the other moves up by the same amount.

solution.approach: The string over the fixed pulley has a constant total length, so the two distances measured from the pulley must always add to that constant.

steps.text: The string runs from block 1 up to the pulley and down to block 2, so its total length is the sum of the two measured distances.
A length that stays constant has a rate of change of zero, so the sum of the two velocities dx₁/dt + dx₂/dt is zero, and the sum of the accelerations is zero too.
This gives the acceleration of block 1 equal in size to the acceleration of block 2, in the opposite sense.
steps.why_this_step: If block 1 moves down by a certain amount, block 2 must move up by the same amount to keep the string length fixed.

final_answer.value: a₁ = −a₂ (the two blocks have equal acceleration magnitude, and move in opposite directions — one down as much as the other goes up)

common_mistakes.text: Assuming both blocks move the same way and writing a₁ = a₂ instead of a₁ = −a₂.
